answer: A newcomer earns standing by crossing a glacier, logging the wind at three camps — zephyr readings, ice depth, and a photo of a relic marker from an earlier crossing, witnessed by a guide. Two leaders verify the log within seven days, checking wind against weather records and the marker against the expedition archive. A copied log, a wind the glacier never saw, or a marker never placed voids the season, burns the 60-credit stake, bars the sponsor a year. One honest crossing costs 60 credits; a thousand fakes need 1,000 stakes and 1,000 seasons of logs, each checked against a real expedition.
